title: A 12-week study plan
lines: Twelve weeks suits you if you are aiming for a big score increase, have been away from math for a while, are building academic English vocabulary, or can only study about an hour a day. The plan moves slowly through the basics, then adds speed and full-length practice. Plan on 1 hour on weekdays and 2-3 hours on one weekend day, roughly 90-100 hours in total.
## Three phases
- Weeks 1-5, foundations: learn every topic with its lesson and practice set.
- Weeks 6-9, strengthening: timed practice, weak topics, regular mocks.
- Weeks 10-12, test readiness: full mocks, stamina, final polish.
! Consistency beats intensity. An hour every day for twelve weeks does far more than three long weekends of cramming.
## Before you start
- Read the articles in "The exam" group so you know the format and scoring.
- Take Mock Test 1 as a baseline, essay included. Do not worry about the score; it is a starting point.
- Set a daily vocabulary goal: about 15 new flashcards a day, which covers the full deck with time for review.
## Week 1: numbers and the logic of Text Completion
- Quant: integers and number properties lesson and practice set.
- Verbal: Text Completion with one blank.
- Read the question types tour article.
## Week 2: fractions, percents and two- and three-blank completions
- Quant: fractions, decimals, percents and ratios.
- Verbal: Text Completion with two and three blanks.
- Essay: read the essay article and write one untimed essay with the template.
## Week 3: exponents and Sentence Equivalence
- Quant: exponents, roots and absolute value.
- Verbal: Sentence Equivalence.
- Redo any practice set from weeks 1-2 that scored below 70%.
## Week 4: algebra and short reading
- Quant: equations and inequalities.
- Verbal: short reading passages.
- Essay: one timed essay; rate it against the model essay.
- Weekend: Mock Test 2.
## Week 5: functions, word problems and long reading
- Quant: functions, quadratics and coordinate geometry; word problems.
- Verbal: long reading passages and argument paragraphs.
- Read the Verbal tips and Quant tips articles.
## Week 6: geometry
- Quant: lines, angles, triangles and polygons; circles, solids and coordinate figures.
- Verbal: one mixed timed practice set every other day.
- Read the time management article and start timing every set.
- Essay: one timed essay.
## Week 7: data, statistics and counting
- Quant: statistics; counting, probability and sets; data interpretation.
- Verbal: redo the two weakest Verbal sets.
- Weekend: Mock Test 3. Compare your topic accuracy with Mock Test 1.
## Week 8: weak topics, round 1
- Take the five weakest topics from the Progress tab. For each: reread the lesson, redo the set, read every explanation.
- Read the guessing and marking article and use the two-pass method in every set.
- Essay: one timed essay.
- Weekend: Mock Test 4.
## Week 9: mixed timed practice
- Daily: one Verbal and one Quant set from different topics, timed.
- Start an error log if you have not already: topic, reason for the error, what to do next time.
- Weekend: Mock Test 5.
## Week 10: stamina
- Two full mocks this week: Mock Tests 6 and 7, at the time of day of your real test.
- Read the test anxiety and stamina article and practice the breathing reset.
- Between mocks, review every wrong answer and every guess.
- Essay: covered inside the mocks.
## Week 11: weak topics, round 2
- Return to the topics still marked weak. Redo sets until you score 80% or higher.
- Mock Test 8 midweek, Mock Test 9 at the weekend.
- Review your vocabulary misses; most of the deck should now feel familiar.
## Week 12: final polish
- Days 1-2: reread your error log and the essay template.
- Day 3: Mock Test 10, your last full mock.
- Days 4-6: light review only. Read the test day article and prepare your ID and route or room.
- Day before the test: rest.
## Keep the plan flexible
- If a topic clicks quickly, move on early and bank the time for a harder one.
- If you fall behind by a week, drop one mock from weeks 10-11 rather than skipping lessons.
- After about ten mocks you still have more in the app; use them for a retake plan if you need one.
